{{Short description|Alleged sex crime in Ithaca, New York, US}} {{pp-semi-indef|small=yes}} {{Use American English|date=September 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=September 2026}} {{Infobox event | image = Cornell - Chi Phi Lodge 3.jpg | image_caption = The [[Chi Phi]] Lodge at Cornell University, (pictured c. 1908) | date = October 19–20, 2024 (incident)
September 16, 2026 (lawsuit) | location = [[Cornell University]], [[Ithaca, New York]] | target = | participants = [[Jane Doe]] (unnamed female student), Cornell University, Chi Phi fraternity, Tompkins County District Attorney's Office | outcome = Active; criminal investigation reopened for grand jury review | inquiries = Cornell University Title IX office investigation | accused = | litigation = Civil lawsuit filed by Doe against Cornell University and seven Chi Phi members (ongoing) | coordinates = {{Coord|42.44366|N|76.4889|W|dim:10_region:US-NY|display=it}} }} On September 16, 2026, an unnamed former student of [[Cornell University]], identified under the pseudonym [[Jane Doe]], sued the university and its [[Chi Phi]] fraternity chapter, including a group of seven students known as the '''Cornell 7''', alleging that she was drugged and [[Gang rape|gang-raped]] by them at a fraternity house in 2024, and that Cornell failed to protect her or punish the alleged perpetrators.{{cite news |title=Timeline of alleged Cornell University fraternity house rape investigation |agency=ABC News |work=JAM Broadcasting |date=October 2, 2026 |url=https://jambroadcasting.com/timeline-of-alleged-cornell-university-fraternity-house-rape-investigation/}}{{Cite web |date=2026-09-29|title='Cornell 7': What happened with the case? What to know as prosecutor reopens investigation|url=https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/local/cornell-7-what-happened-with-the-case-what-to-know-as-prosecutor-reopens-investigation/3995362/|access-date=2026-09-29|website=[[WMAQ-TV|NBC Chicago]]|language=en-US|agency=[[Associated Press]]|last=Stechyson|first=Natalie}}{{Cite web |last=Reinhart|first=Max|title=Michigan man among 7 accused in alleged Cornell fraternity gang rape|url=https://www.detroitnews.com/story/news/local/michigan/2026/09/29/cornell-gang-rape-case-defendants-include-michigan-high-school-graduate/92009060007/|access-date=2026-10-01|website=The Detroit News|language=en-US}}{{Cite web |title=Cornell, Chi Phi Sued by Victim of Alleged Gang Rape, Drugging in 2024|url=https://www.cornellsun.com/article/2026/09/tccsuykuvb4z|access-date=2026-10-01|website=The Cornell Daily Sun|language=en-US}} The case has attracted national media and political attention in 2026 following a civil lawsuit by the alleged victim. A [[Title IX]] investigation conducted by Cornell University resulted in two of the students being expelled by Cornell. According to the lawsuit, all seven had been temporarily suspended and given an "opportunity to mitigate their conduct by submitting essays to Cornell", though Cornell has stated that none of them were offered essays as a "sole consequence".{{Cite news |last=Fernández|first=Jasmine|date=2026-09-28|title=Ex-Cornell student sues fraternity members and college over alleged gang rape and claims several were punished with essay-writing|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/cornell-university-sexual-assault-lawsuit-b3057169.html|work=[[The |title=District Attorney statement re: Jane Doe v. Cornell University, et al |url=https://www.tompkinscountyny.gov/News-articles/District-Attorney-statement-regarding-Jane-Doe-v.-Cornell-University-et-al |access-date=2026-10-02 |website=tompkinscountyny.gov |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260929085033/https://www.tompkinscountyny.gov/News-articles/District-Attorney-statement-regarding-Jane-Doe-v.-Cornell-University-et-al |archive-date=September 29, 2026 |url-status=live}} Following media outcry, New York governor [[Kathy Hochul]] called for a transparent and independent review of Cornell's responses and appointed Attorney General [[Letitia James]] as a [[special prosecutor]].{{cite web |last1=Charalambous|first1=Peter|last2=Rubin|first2=Olivia|last3=Wilson|first3=Courtney|last4=Katersky|first4=Aaron|date=2026-09-29|title=District attorney reopens case of alleged Cornell University 'gang rape'|url=https://abcnews.com/US/district-attorney-reopens-case-alleged-cornell-university-gang/story?id=136806149|access-date=2026-09-29|website=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]|language=en-US|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260929182040/https://abcnews.com/US/district-attorney-reopens-case-alleged-cornell-university-gang/story?id=136806149|archive-date=September 29, 2026|url-status=live}} == Alleged gang rape == At around 8:30 p.m. on October 19, 2024, a 20-year-old student at Cornell University and member of the [[Delta Delta Delta]] sorority attended a sorority social event at Moonies Bar & Nightclub in [[Ithaca, New York]]. She had drunk vodka at her sorority house before travelling to the bar with the chapter's house mother. She alleged that the bar staff were aware that she was below the [[legal drinking age in the United States]] (21), drawing an "X" mark on both of her hands to indicate this, but she was still provided with at least one drink at the establishment. She and her sorority co-members walked to another bar. According to Doe, by 11 p.m., she had drunk approximately ten drinks in three hours. She was "visibly drunk." She walked about 1 mile from the bar to visit a male friend, a member of the school's Chi Phi chapter, at the fraternity house.{{Cite news | first=Chris | last=Kenning | date=September 30, 2026 | title=Cornell rape case explained: Allegations, investigation, lawsuit | url=https://eu.usatoday.com/story/news/nation/2026/09/30/cornell-7-jane-doe-rape-case-timeline/92003702007/ | work=[[USA Today]] | language=en-US | access-date=October 1, 2026 | archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/RwZmW | archive-date=October 1, 2026 | url-status=live}} According to Doe, the male friend took her inside the fraternity house, gave her another beer, and proposed a [[threesome]] with a second man. She reportedly developed bruising and said she was pressured to consume [[ketamine]]. She alleged that it was her first time consuming the drug.{{Cite news | first1=Shayna | last1=Jacobs | first2=Pilar | last2=Melendez | title=Records give insight into how one Cornell student responded to rape accusation | url=https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/investigative-records-give-insight-accused-cornell-student-responded-a-rcna600987 | date=October 2, 2026 | access-date=October 2, 2026 | publisher=[[NBC News]] | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261001235924/https://www.nbcnews.com/news/us-news/investigative-records-give-insight-accused-cornell-student-responded-a-rcna600987 | archive-date=October 1, 2026 | url-status=live}} Before any sexual acts took place with these two men, she additionally consumed [[marijuana]] and [[rum]]. By the following day, at around 1:42 a.m., some of the men exchanged [[Snapchat]] messages in a group chat called "Chi Phi Actives" saying that there was "free pussy upstairs", allegedly in reference to Doe. At one point, a photo of Doe was sent to the chat, in which she appeared to be smiling with a man; immediately before this, one man allegedly wrote, "Like you can walk in and whip it out." Another man also allegedly asked "Shop still open?" immediately after this image was sent, receiving an affirmative reply.{{Cite news | first1=Tom | last1=Hanson | first2=Mark | last2=Osborne | date=October 2, 2026 | title=Picture of Jane Doe shared in Snapchat group on night of alleged Cornell rape | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jane-doe-photo-cornell-rape-snapchat-group/ | publisher=[[CBS News]] | language=en-US | access-date=October 2, 2026 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261002160338/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jane-doe-photo-cornell-rape-snapchat-group/ | archive-date=October 2, 2026 | url-status=live }} In response to the photo, an unknown individual also asked, "Are you guys at least naked?". The texts are said to have been leaked by a Chi Phi member who was "outraged" by the alleged abuse. According to the lawsuit, she lost consciousness at around 5:45 a.m. on October 20. === 2024 police report === Doe told police that she was "pretty OK" with the first encounter.{{Cite news | first1=Mark | last1=Osborne | first2=Paula | last2=Cohen | date=October 1, 2026 | title=Jane Doe's account of what happened at Cornell frat, from text messages and investigators' transcripts | url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/jane-doe-cornell-university-rape-allegations-text-messages-transcripts/ | publisher=[[CBS News]] | language=en-US | access-date=October 2, 2026 }} According to the district attorney's summary of Doe's police statement, the first threesome ended when one of the men lost his erection and "stumbled" from the couch to the bed to take a nap and the second man began dry-heaving. Doe comforted him, but he assured her that he would not vomit. They briefly kissed again, with the man allegedly reaching for the area near her vagina "several" times. She allegedly swatted his hand away each time.{{Cite web |title=District Attorney statement re: Jane Doe v. Cornell University, et al |url=https://www.tompkinscountyny.gov/News-articles/District-Attorney-statement-regarding-Jane-Doe-v.-Cornell-University-et-al |access-date=October 2, 2026 |website=Tompkins County |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260929085033/https://www.tompkinscountyny.gov/News-articles/District-Attorney-statement-regarding-Jane-Doe-v.-Cornell-University-et-al |archive-date=September 29, 2026 |url-status=live}} She permitted a third man to enter the room because it was his room. Doe and the third man kissed, eventually engaging in a second threesome with the second man as the first continued sleeping nearby. The first man eventually woke up and proposed a foursome, to which Doe said "Hell no", and it didn't proceed. At one point, the third man left the room. Four other men then entered the room. According to Doe, she was "horrified" when these additional men entered the room and hid under the covers of the bed.{{Cite news | first=KC | last=Baker | date=October 1, 2026 | title=Cornell Accuser Said She Was 'Instantly Horrified' When More Men Entered Frat Room: Investigation | url=https://people.com/cornell-accuser-said-she-was-instantly-horrified-when-more-men-entered-frat-room-investigation-12151659 | magazine=[[People (magazine)|People]] | language=en-US | access-date=October 3, 2026 }} The first man was described as sitting on the corner of the bed and allegedly introduced the other men to Doe. A third threesome occurred between the first man and one of the four additional men in another room of the house, and the three also consumed additional alcohol and ketamine. The third threesome ended when Doe said she was "tired". === 2026 civil complaint === The 2026 complaint recounted the same events as Doe's 2024 police account, but alleged that she was "incapable of consenting" to the initial encounter; she previously told police she had been "pretty OK" with it. Both accounts alleged rape during the later encounters. === Men's accounts === According to investigative records obtained by ''[[The New York Times]]'', four of the accused men acknowledged sexual contact with Doe but alleged that it was consensual; the others denied participating in sexual encounters. One alleged that Doe had performed oral sex on him when he was too incapacitated to consent. The ''Times'' reported that their accounts differed and frequently contradicted one another.{{cite news |last1=Coleman |first1=Maia |last2=Fahy |first2=Claire |title=Men Accused in Cornell Sex Assault Suit Give Varying Accounts of Night |agency=The New York Times |work=GV Wire |date=October 1, 2026 |url=https://gvwire.com/2026/10/01/men-accused-in-cornell-sex-assault-suit-give-varying-accounts-of-night/}} Most of the men alleged that Doe did not appear intoxicated. One participant in the initial threesome said he assumed her friend had obtained her consent, and that he and her friend had drunk heavily, used marijuana and ketamine, and vomited. Another alleged that Doe initiated sexual contact without asking for his consent. He said he later asked her permission for a threesome and she allegedly replied, "We're all consenting adults here." Two others said they entered after reading the Snapchat message; one claimed that they were checking on Doe's welfare. Another man denied using drugs or engaging in sexual contact and said that he only stayed in the room Doe was in for five minutes. Another man said he was initially concerned on entering after 2:30 a.m., but was reassured when those present invited him in. == Aftermath == In documents from Cornell's [[Title IX]] investigation, one of Doe's roommates testified that in the morning after the incident, she was seemingly in shock and trying to laugh off what had transpired. According to another roommate, Doe told her, "I wasn't comfortable." On October 21, one of the accused men texted her to apologize for "how things went down" and said his memory was "kinda fuzzy". Doe replied that "non{{Sic}} of the sexual stuff was illegal" and that she had liked being with him and the other man in the initial encounter. She also said that her memory was "super clouded too", assured him that they were amicable, and suggested that they could smoke substances together again, though she requested to "leave out the extra 5 billion men and ketamine". On October 22, Doe told a university doctor that she had contracted a [[urinary tract infection]] "in a traumatic way" and sought testing for [[sexually transmitted diseases]]; allegedly, she was advised to "speak with somebody" and was not offered expert consultation or a [[rape kit]].{{Cite news | date=October 1, 2026 | first1=Madeline | last1=Halpert | first2=Kayla | last2=Epstein | first3=Nada | last3=Tawfik | title=Cornell accuser was 'failed' by university health care system, lawyer says |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c699d93j22r5o | access-date=October 1, 2026 | work=[[BBC News]] |language=en}}{{Cite news | first=Lauren | last=Mascarenhas | date=October 1, 2026 | title=A 'loophole' in New York's rape law may have shut the door on criminal charges in the Cornell case. It's not the first time |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2026/10/01/us/ny-rape-law-loophole-cornell | access-date=October 1, 2026 | publisher=[[CNN]] |language=en-US}} The Title IX record contains an interview with one of the accused men where he allegedly confirmed that he spoke to Doe, convincing her not to "spread any rumors" about the incident. He is also quoted as saying that he and his fraternity co-members were "in the idea of just deny" if asked about the events of that night.{{Cite news | date=October 2, 2026 | first=KC | last=Baker | title=Man Accused in Cornell Rape Case Said Frat Brothers' Approach Was 'Just Deny': Transcript |url=https://people.com/cornell-rape-case-suspect-said-frat-brothers-approach-was-just-deny-transcript-12154595 | access-date=October 2, 2026 | magazine=[[People (magazine)|People]] |language=en-US}} Doe maintained friendly correspondence with her male friend until a week following the incident, when she read a comment in an online forum about the fraternity, referring to people who had "gang raped a sophomore".{{Cite news |last=Otterman |first=Sharon |date=2026-10-01 |title=The Cornell Rape Investigation: Five Takeaways |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/01/nyregion/cornell-jane-doe-rape-investigation-documents.html |access-date=2026-10-02 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} Her male friend had assured her that she was welcome at the fraternity's annual Halloween party, which she had been eager to attend. However, before Halloween, the fraternity's president phoned Doe to inform her that she was disinvited from the party.{{Cite news |last1=Kamin |first1=Debra |last2=Flegenheimer |first2=Matt |last3=Harris |first3=Amy Julia |last4=Otterman |first4=Sharon |date=2026-10-01 |title=How a Cornell Student Went From Shame to Action |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/01/nyregion/cornell-rape-accusation-reporting.html |access-date=2026-10-02 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}} On November 3, she texted two of the accused men and alleged that "90% of what happened that night was not consensual". On November 7, Doe went to an emergency room in Ithaca and requested a rape kit. On November 8, 2024, Doe reported these alleged assaults to Cornell University Police. == 2024–2025 initial investigation == Doe was first interviewed by the Cornell University Police from November 14 to 15, 2024.{{Cite news | first=Mahsa | last=Saeidi | title=Jane Doe in Cornell University case told campus police, "I can say with 100% confidence I was raped," transcript shows |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/cornell-university-rape-case-jane-doe-police-interview-transcript/ | access-date=October 1, 2026 | publisher=[[CBS News]] |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260930175345/https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/cornell-university-rape-case-jane-doe-police-interview-transcript/ |archive-date=September 30, 2026 |url-status=live}} This reportedly produced a 120-page transcript, which was obtained by [[CBS News]] in 2026. They quoted Doe as saying, "I can say with 100% confidence I was raped." and providing detailed accusations within the document. After receiving a six-page summary of Doe's statement prepared by campus police in 2024, Tompkins County [[district attorney]] [[Matthew Van Houten]] declined to present the case to a [[grand jury]].{{Cite news | first=Hurubie | last=Meko | date=October 1, 2026 | title=Cornell Police Report Omitted Student's Claim She Was Raped | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/01/nyregion/url-cornell-university-jane-doe-rape-case-statement.html | access-date=October 1, 2026 | newspaper=[[The New York Times]] | language=en-US | url-status=live | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261001164318/https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/01/nyregion/url-cornell-university-jane-doe-rape-case-statement.html | archive-date=October 1, 2026}} In September 2026, he said he had not seen the full police transcript when he made his previous decision and claimed that the condensed version had described the accuser's "participation" as "voluntary, conscious, and consensual."{{Cite web |date=2026-09-28 |title=District Attorney statement re: Jane Doe v. Cornell University, et al |url=https://www.tompkinscountyny.gov/News-articles/District-Attorney-statement-regarding-Jane-Doe-v.-Cornell-University-et-al |access-date=2026-09-30 |website=[[Tompkins County, New York]] |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260929085033/https://www.tompkinscountyny.gov/News-articles/District-Attorney-statement-regarding-Jane-Doe-v.-Cornell-University-et-al |archive-date=September 29, 2026 |url-status=live}} However, within this condensed version, [[NPR]]'s Jaclyn Diaz noted "several" instances of Doe saying that she did not consent to certain activities and was "increasingly" intoxicated as the evening progressed.{{Cite news | first=Jaclyn | last=Diaz | title=Police questioning can shape a sexual assault case. Their approach is often wrong | url=https://www.npr.org/2026/09/30/nx-s1-5983868/cornell-rape-police-interview-investigation-victim-trauma-informed | date=September 1, 2026 | access-date=October 1, 2026 | publisher=[[NPR]] |language=en-US |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260930204457/https://www.npr.org/2026/09/30/nx-s1-5983868/cornell-rape-police-interview-investigation-victim-trauma-informed |archive-date=September 30, 2026 |url-status=live}} According to ''[[The New York Times]]'', the police-prepared summary retained Doe's allegations that she "felt some of that night's events were a crime" but omitted "some of the more forceful and definitive language she used," including her explicit assertion that she had been raped. Cornell commenced a formal [[Title IX]] investigation on January 14, 2025. Subsequently, the office conducted at least twelve hearings addressing Doe's accusations in May 2025. For one of the hearings, Cornell prepared a 99-page report regarding the incident. Investigators reportedly conducted 50 interviews with 32 witnesses. They determined that [[ketamine]] had been in use at the fraternity in the week of the incident and one individual had overdosed on the drug at the Chi Phi house one day before Doe was allegedly raped.{{Cite news | first=Katherine | last=Schaffstall | title=Cornell University Gang Rape Victim Said She 'Felt Like Bait' During 2025 Hearing About Assault | url=https://www.usmagazine.com/crime-news/news/cornell-university-gang-rape-victim-felt-like-bait/ | date=October 1, 2026 | access-date=October 1, 2026 | magazine=[[Us Weekly]] | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20261001201558/https://www.usmagazine.com/crime-news/news/cornell-university-gang-rape-victim-felt-like-bait/ | archive-date=October 1, 2026 | url-status=live}} One of them allegedly entered the room following the Snapchat message and left after consuming ketamine off of Doe's body. He was found responsible by the Title IX investigation for "attempted sexual exploitation" but not sexual assault. During the hearing, he made an apology towards Doe: "I was sorry that maybe if it wasn't consensual and she was victimized, I was sorry for not stopping it. And that I'm sorry I couldn't tell if she was under the influence… just sorry that I felt like if something actually bad happened, I didn't stop it." === 2025 outcomes === Among the seven accused men, two were expelled; another two were suspended for at least two semesters; one had already graduated before any punishment could be given; and two were declared as not responsible for sexual misconduct. None were arrested. Although he was not among the two who were expelled, one of the men faced several sanctions including: writing a reflection paper about his involvement in the alleged sexual abuse; writing a "detailed proposal" for future educational material at Cornell; and participating in a study at the [[Office of Civil Rights]] about social media use, [[sexual harassment]] and bystander intervention. He was also forbidden from speaking to Doe. He later filed a petition to annul Cornell's decision, arguing that it was "unfair"; his appeal was denied in early 2026. The failed petition publicized details relevant to his involvement in the case. Among these details, Cornell's investigative panel concluded in its May hearing that his Snapchat message on the night of the incident indicated understanding of a "sexual situation involving a female" when he chose to enter the room; and that the record supported the finding that he was responsible for "attempted sexual exploitation". They did not find sufficient evidence that he had been using ketamine. During the alleged gang rape, he had gone upstairs upon receiving the "free pussy" message and later told the chat's other members that it was "not a bit" upon confirming Doe's presence in the room. "I shouldn't have said it. And it is immature and a stupid text message for sure," he had stated at the hearing, insisting that he had merely been "following along with what everyone else was saying". == 2026 civil lawsuit and criminal investigation == In September 2026, Van Houten said he would consider presenting the case to a grand jury despite his refusal to do so in 2024.{{cite news |last1=Otterman |first1=Sharon |date=2026-09-29 |title=What We Know About the Cornell Rape Investigation |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/29/nyregion/cornell-university-rape-investigation-chi-phi-fraternity.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260929233112/https://www.nytimes.com/2026/09/29/nyregion/cornell-university-rape-investigation-chi-phi-fraternity.html |archive-date=September 29, 2026
